title: Report says Trump directed McGahn to seek Mueller’s removal
description_medium: On January 25, 2018, The New York Times reported that President Donald Trump had directed White House Counsel Don McGahn to tell the Justice Department to remove Special Counsel Robert Mueller in June 2017. McGahn did not relay the request and decided he would resign rather than carry it out. Trump disputed the reporting the next day. Mueller’s later report examined the episode in its obstruction inquiry.
description_long: The New York Times reported on January 25, 2018, that President Donald Trump had directed White House Counsel Don McGahn to have Special Counsel Robert Mueller removed the previous June. According to that account, Trump wanted McGahn to ask the Justice Department to dismiss Mueller; McGahn did not deliver the request and decided he would resign rather than take part. The report emerged while Mueller was investigating Russian interference in the 2016 election and possible obstruction of justice. Trump rejected the story as “fake news” the next day. The Justice Department’s 2019 Mueller report later confirmed that Trump called McGahn on June 17, 2017, and directed him to contact the acting attorney general, say Mueller had conflicts of interest, and secure Mueller’s removal. McGahn did not carry out the direction. The report said substantial evidence supported the conclusion that Trump had gone beyond asking officials to review alleged conflicts and sought Mueller’s removal. It also recorded that, after the January 2018 coverage, McGahn would not deny the accounts because he believed they were accurate. The episode became a public controversy in January 2018 and was later examined in the Mueller report, which set McGahn’s account alongside Trump’s denial and the evidence it considered. Mueller’s report was an investigative account, not a court judgment on criminal liability.

title.corrected: Report says Trump directed McGahn to seek Mueller’s removal
title.reason: The entry date is the 2018 report; the described directive was alleged to have occurred in June 2017, and Trump disputed the report.

source_access_notes: Read the Justice Department clemency record and archived White House or contemporaneous reporting for the event. For the McGahn episode, also read Mueller report Volume II.
rationale: The January 25 report concerned an alleged June 2017 directive; Trump denied the account. The later Mueller report discussed McGahn’s recollection and the president’s effort to have him deny the reported direction.
